messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert P1 -> 48721: High 5xx rate from customer 'AstraCorp' on private VPC deployment (dedicated pool eu-west-1). Affected routes: /v1/generate. Paging on-call.
Samir: I'm on it. seeing ~50% 502/504s from the dedicated pool for that tenant. Errors started ~12:07 UTC. Root cause not obvious yet. Traffic looks normal upstream, but targets are failing health checks at the NLB layer.
Maria: Pinged the customer's network lead (Hudson) via email but cc'd them here. Hudson, can you confirm if any recent egress/SG changes were applied on AstraCorp side? We suspect something blocking ephemeral ports between NLB and target instances.
Hudson: hey team — we rolled a tightened SG policy for compliance this morning but it should only affect admin CIDRs. I'll check ASAP. Notified infra team.
Iris-oncall: quick ask — is customer on Dedicated ingress (NLB) with cross-zone enabled? If yes, NLB source IPs vary per AZ.
Samir: yes, dedicated NLB with cross-zone on. Health-checks are 502 at the target level. Logs show connection resets from client side. Sample from nginx on target: "connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while reading response header". Could be SG or host-level firewall.
Maria: adding some basic diagnostics here. Can someone run a curl to the target health endpoint from the NLB? We don't have direct NLB host access but we can curl via the proxy in the same subnet.
Samir: running now from a bastion in same subnet:

# from bastion
curl -sv http://10.10.45.21:8080/health
* Connected to 10.10.45.21 (10.10.45.21) port 8080 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: 10.10.45.21
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< Connection: close

Samir: target app is returning 502 even to local subnet. tcpdump shows SYN then RST from kernel within host. Could be conntrack limit or IPTables reject.
Hudson: We're seeing an automated rule expand this morning that tightened conntrack timeouts and bumped netfilter defaults. I'll back that out for the tenant if you think conntrack is the issue.
Iris-oncall: do we have evidence? What's current conntrack count and limit? Samir, can you paste /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count and _max?
Samir: here's quick dump:

cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
=> 245760
cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
=> 262144

Samir: we're at ~94% of conntrack table for the target host. That'll cause new connections to be dropped (RST). Matches symptom.
Maria: That would definitely produce 502s at the NLB -> targets. Good catch.
Hudson: rolling back the compliance rule now for AstraCorp's subnets, reverting the conntrack tune. ETA 3 minutes.
deploy-bot: CodeDeploy deployment 2345 -> complete to pool:dedicated-eu-west-1 (not related) :white_check_mark:
Samir: while rollback is in progress, we can mitigate by shifting tenant traffic to fallback pool in another dedicated cluster. Suggest updating routing policy to point AstraCorp DNS to fallback target group for 5-10 minutes while they revert.
Iris-oncall: +1. Maria, can you coordinate DNS low-TTL and the routing change? We should also open a support ticket with AstraCorp for a postmortem on config drift.
Maria: I'll do DNS. Lowering TTL to 30s now and creating a temporary CNAME to fallback-nlb-eu-west-1.elb.amazonaws.com. Command:

# update route53 record (example)
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZ --change-batch '{
  "Comment": "temp failover",
  "Changes": [{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{
    "Name":"api.astracorp.internal.","Type":"CNAME","TTL":30,
    "ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"fallback-nlb-eu-west-1.elb.amazonaws.com."}]
  }}]
}'

Maria: change submitted, request ID: C-abc123. Expect propagation ~30s.
Samir: confirming fallback pool health checks are green. Starting traffic shift via routing policy toggle.
Samir: toggled to fallback at 12:22:07 UTC. Observing metrics… 1 minute in and 5xxs drop to <1%.
Hudson: rollback of conntrack change confirmed on AstraCorp side at 12:24 UTC. They reverted the automation that bumped nf_conntrack behavior.
Iris-oncall: nice. Let's gradually shift traffic back and monitor.
Samir: shifting 20% back now, health looks stable. 100% back at 12:30 UTC. Post-rollback verification: conntrack_count now 43k vs max 262k.
Maria: DNS TTL remains low; leave for 10m to ensure stability. Creating incident ticket and linking runbook.
Maria: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/vpc-egress-diagnostics (added notes: conntrack exhaustion from customer-side automation, temporary failover to fallback pool, DNS TTL adjustment, required customer change window)
Iris-oncall: action items before we close:
- Hudson: ensure automation not re-applied; schedule change window and document expected conntrack tuning. (Hudson: ack)
- Samir: add a health-check alert to detect conntrack saturation pattern (high conntrack_count + spikes in 502). (Samir: ack)
- Maria: post-incident customer brief and RCA with AstraCorp; include prevention suggestions (monitoring, non-blocking rules, ephemeral port allowances). (Maria: ack)
Samir: logs and packet captures uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/48721/ — made available to AstraCorp engineers.
Hudson: thanks all. We'll follow up with a plan to widen ephemeral port ranges and add guardrails to infra automation.
Iris-oncall: marking incident as resolved at 12:42 UTC. Will keep thread open for any follow-ups. :white_check_mark: :tada:
Samir: closing monitoring alert. Leaving notes in the on-call doc.
Maria: creating a scheduled postmortem doc and invite for next-day 09:00 UTC. Invite sent to AstraCorp and internal owners.
